[RFCS.15.4] **Classification and versioning.** `CallIssued` is a **compare**
atom ([RFCS.3.4]): never injected, byte-compared on replay
([LFST.9.3.1]). Because it is never a replay input, an older runtime that
does not recognise the `CallIssued` field number **skips it via the length prefix
([RFCS.2.3]) and replays bit-identically** — losing provenance, not
correctness. Registering `CallIssued` is therefore additive: an older reader skips it and
replays correctly, so it needs no release of its own ([LDET.1.10]). This is the
skip-don't-reject precedent of `RuleFireAnnotation` and the planning atoms, and the
inverse of a new inject-class atom, which an old reader must reject
([RFCS.3.4]).
